 Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Reaves, who did not play in Monday’s win over the Hawks, returns and will take on his usual role within the Lakers’ lineup. Ziaire Williams heads to the bench, while the other four starters are unchanged.

 Lakers head coach JJ Redick said ahead of Tuesday’s game against the Hornets that Austin Reaves will get on the court Wednesday to test his injured heel. 
 Tuesday’s game will be the second Reaves has missed since injuring his left heel during a November 11 win over the Bucks. The plan is for him to take the court Wednesday to test his heel and see how he feels. Quentin Grimes should remain in the starting lineup for as long as Reaves is out. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Austin Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Reaves will remain out for a second game due to this heel injury, and there isn’t a clear timeline as to how long he’ll end up being sidelined. Until he’s back, Quentin Grimes will continue to start, especially after he had 22 points and five triples in 37 minutes on Sunday. 
 Adou Thiero 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Adou Thiero (ankle) is questionable to play against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Thiero has been a rotation piece for the Lakers since making his season debut last Thursday. His status for this game is up in the air, and he could take on a larger role if he plays since Austin Reaves (heel) is out. Ziaire Williams would play extra minutes if Thiero is out. 
 Collin Sexton

 #10 
 Collin Sexton (eye) is questionable to play against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Sexton should be in line to take on extra minutes with Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined. However, if he’s out, Adou Thiero, who is also questionable, or Ziaire Williams could be in line to fill out the extra minutes.

 Austin Reaves (heel) has been ruled out against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Reaves exited early from Wednesday’s win, and he’ll remain out despite getting a few days off between games. Quentin Grimes will be back following a two-game absence and should get the starting nod with Reaves sidelined.

 Austin Reaves (heel) missed practice on Saturday. 
 Reaves is dealing with a heel bruise. The 28-year-old guard missed practice Saturday, though it’s unclear if he’ll miss any game time. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 ESPN’s Dave McMenamin reports that Austin Reaves is listed as day-to-day with a bruised heel. 
 According to head coach JJ Redick, Reaves and the Lakers medical staff opted against imaging. This latest update is favorable for the severity of the injury, and Reaves could miss little time, if any at all. If Reaves is forced to sit out, Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes could pick up the slack. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić (ankle) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 32 points (10-of-25 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and five three-pointers. 
 Dončić has scored at least 30 points in each of his last nine appearances. However, there was a concerning moment when the Lakers star appeared to tweak his ankle during the fourth quarter. The benches were being cleared at this point, so Dončić returned to the Lakers’ locker room with a team trainer with 4:23 remaining in the fourth quarter. We’ll see if he lands on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Spurs, especially with Austin Reaves (heel) leaving Wednesday’s victory during the third quarter.

 The Lakers were already up double digits, so there was no need to bring him back in. If he is to miss time, look for Collin Sexton to take more shots and more minutes for Quentin Grimes. They both become stream options in redraft leagues but not high priority ones.

 Austin Reaves (illness) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Reaves did not play in Monday’s win over the Hawks. With Quentin Grimes also out, Ziaire Williams returned to the starting lineup. Either Williams or Jake LaRavia is likely to come off the bench on Wednesday.

 Jrue Holiday accounted for 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 With Deni Avdija ruled out, the Trail Blazers needed someone to step up offensively. Holiday was still used in a reserve role, but his 19 shot attempts tied him with Damian Lillard for the most on the team. Jrue finished with a full line, and he’s become a bit more valuable to fantasy managers since Ja Morant strained his hamstring. Jayson Kent started for Avdija, finishing with eight points, three rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Donovan Clingan tallied 12 points (6-of-14 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Clingan wasn’t dominant against the Timberwolves, but he still thoroughly outplayed Rudy Gobert. The Trail Blazers’ center finished with his third straight double-double, and he’s recorded double-digit rebounds in five straight games. Add in the assists, and Clingan’s stat line may help compensate for the percentages.

 Damian Lillard finished Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
 Lillard finished with 25 points, but his layup attempt in the final seconds, which would have given Portland the win, was blocked by Minnesota’s Trey Lyles. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of the 10 games Portland has played since losing Ja Morant to a hamstring injury, providing top-100 fantasy value. Portland visits Milwaukee on Thursday in Lillard’s first game against the Bucks since being waived in the summer of 2025.

 LaMelo Ball recorded 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
 After recording at least five assists in five straight games, Ball had two in the Timberwolves’ two games against Portland. The good news for the Timberwolves was that they won both games, but that low assist number was a surprise. Ball finished Tuesday’s win one rebound shy of a double-double, offering unexpected value in that category. Even with the recent low assist numbers, field-goal percentage and turnovers remain Ball’s biggest issues in category leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaden McDaniels amassed 22 points (10-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
 While McDaniels’ offensive production has been consistent throughout the season, fantasy managers may have hoped for a bit more from him in the aftermath of Anthony Edwards’ knee injury. He’s scored 20+ points three times since Edwards was injured in an October 26 loss to the Cavaliers, and his 23 points against the Trail Blazers matched his season high. That said, even with the scoring, McDaniels is still providing top-50 value in category leagues.

 Ayo Dosunmu accounted for 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
 After scoring eight points on 3-of-11 shooting in Monday’s win over the Trail Blazers, Dosunmu rebounded in a big way in Tuesday’s rematch. Making his 10th straight start for the injured Anthony Edwards, Ayo recorded his first 30-point stat line of the season while shooting a high percentage from the field. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was an excellent night for those rostering Dosunmu.

 Already playing without Austin Reaves, the Lakers won’t have Walker Kessler for Tuesday’s game. Looney moves into the starting lineup, and while he can provide rebounds in that role, Sandro Mamukelashvili is the superior fantasy option despite coming off the bench.

 Coby White, Brandon Miller, Grant Williams, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté will start Tuesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Hornets head coach Charles Lee has changed his starting lineup, with Williams replacing Sion James. Williams played 20 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers, hitting three three-pointers and scoring 11 points. While a solid defender, James is limited as a scorer, which may have factored into the lineup change.

 Stephon Castle recorded 10 points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons.
 Castle didn’t have a good night shooting the basketball, but he did provide solid value in the assists column. He has recorded six or more assists in three of his last four games and is averaging 5.5 assists per game for the season. De’Aaron Fox (6/2/2/2) also struggled against the Pistons, shooting 3-of-10 from the field, offering even less value to fantasy managers than Castle. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Devin Vassell finished Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons with 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 A 2-of-4 night from beyond the arc isn’t much, but it was a step in the right direction for Vassell, who was 0-of-6 in wins over the Warriors and Jazz. A career 37.0 percent shooter from three, Devin entered Tuesday making a career-low 31.4 percent of his attempts. Fantasy managers rostering Vassell received solid value in rebounds and assists on Tuesday, but consistent three-point shooting is key for him.
